in-county-government.summary: The County card lists every member of your county's governing bodies but not which district seat is yours.
in-county-government.why: Neither the commissioners' nor the council's district lines are on this app's map yet, so the card lists every seat rather than yours. In Marion County the same is true of the Indianapolis City-County Council.
in-county-government.wanted: The commissioner and council district covering the point, and in Marion County the City-County Council district.

in-general-assembly-roster.summary: Both General Assembly cards name your district and link the chamber's directory instead of naming your senator or representative.
in-general-assembly-roster.why: This app has not yet fetched a roster for either chamber, so it sends you to the General Assembly's own member list rather than printing a name it cannot check.
in-general-assembly-roster.wanted: The senator and representative holding each of the 50 Senate and 100 House districts.

in-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City or Town card names the mayor and council only in places over 25,000 people, and not which council seat is yours.
in-municipal-officeholders.why: This app reads the state's election results for Indiana's largest places so far. Three of those are towns whose uncontested seats are on no ballot, and council district lines are not on the map, so the card lists every seat.
in-municipal-officeholders.wanted: The mayor or town council president, the council members and the clerk of each city and town, and the council district covering the point.

in-school-board-members.summary: The School District card names the district and none of the board members who run it.
in-school-board-members.why: Indiana elects most school board members, but this app has no roster of them and no map of the seats that are elected by district, so it names the district only.
in-school-board-members.wanted: The board members of each district, and the sub-district boundaries where a seat is elected by one.

in-township-officers.summary: The Township card names your township and none of the four or six people you elect to run it.
in-township-officers.why: An Indiana township elects a trustee and a township board, and some also elect an assessor. This app draws the township and has not yet fetched who holds those offices.
in-township-officers.wanted: The trustee, the board members and, where one is elected, the assessor of each township.
